note: site selector <-> plugin selector. The parity contract. Add a pair when a surface is ported.
ownsNote: A pair with no "owns" compares EVERY rule. "owns" exists for one situation: the plugin collapses two site nodes into one node, so different rule families have different honest counterparts (e.g. the site's section head is a text-less flex WRAPPER holding a .tag; the plugin's .dse-section__title is BOTH). Splitting the pair lets the box/material rules aim at the wrapper and the type/ink rules aim at the real text. It is NOT a mute button: compare.cjs REFUSES TO RUN unless, for EVERY plugin selector -- shared by two pairs or named by only one -- the owned sets cover the full rule list exactly once. A rule may be MOVED to a sibling pair, never dropped in silence, never double-counted. The one way to drop a rule is an explicit "excludes": [{ rule, why }] entry on the narrowing pair, priced exactly like a declared deferral (its "why" must cite a workspace FOLLOWUPS number or a Linear ticket) -- and gated the same way too: a MATERIAL rule (bg, bg-polarity, bg-color, shadow, hairline-top, hairline-bottom) can never be excluded any more than it can be declared away; fix the CSS, or move the rule to the sibling pair that measures it honestly. Nothing in the shipped map uses "excludes" today. Valid rule names: bg, bg-polarity, bg-color, shadow, hairline-top, hairline-bottom, font-size, line-height, padding-top, padding-right, padding-bottom, padding-left, margin-top, margin-bottom, body-font, letter-spacing, ink.
declaredDeferralsNote: THE ONLY thing that keeps a finding from failing the gate. Shape: { pair, rule, scheme?, why }. A declaration converts a matching GAP or WARN row into a DECLARED row; everything else is fatal, so the contract is exit 0 iff 0 GAPs AND 0 undeclared WARNs. compare.cjs enforces five things mechanically: the pair must exist; the rule must be a real rule name; the rule must not be MATERIAL (bg, bg-polarity, bg-color, shadow, hairline-top, hairline-bottom are NON-DECLARABLE -- a flat surface, a missing bevel or a missing hairline is always closable in styles-source.css, and a wholly flat Steel theme that passed human review is the exact failure this gate was built to catch; geometry, typography and ink stay declarable, because that is where real pixel decisions live); the pair must actually OWN that rule (or the declaration could never match); and "why" must cite a workspace FOLLOWUPS number or a Linear ticket (a real one -- SC-0 / FOLLOWUPS #0 are rejected). The capture rules are DIRECTIONAL: declare "capture-site" for a site page that legitimately does not carry the node, "capture-plugin" for a plugin node that never rendered; neither silences the other. diff.mjs additionally FAILS on a declaration that matched nothing this run -- a stale excuse for a finding that has since been fixed. A declaration is never a way to silence something CSS can close; deleting or weakening a pair is never acceptable either.

declaredDeferrals.why: FOLLOWUPS #40 / SC-110 -- DELIBERATE divergence, not a measurement artifact. The site splits its power-roll caption into .pre (dim metal, 'Power Roll +') and .chars (the bright roll readout); the plugin's .dse-pr__head is ONE node carrying the whole caption, painted at var(--dse-heading) so the line reads as a heading. That is brighter than the site's .chars in dark (220,226,230 @.95 vs 205,209,212) and darker in light (26,29,32 vs 95,104,109) -- more emphasis, both schemes, by design. Matching .chars exactly would de-emphasise the plugin's only power-roll heading. Changing it is a PIXEL decision for Scott, not a CSS catch-up.

SC-235 -- DELIBERATE divergence, option B (Scott's ruling, comment 00d1a795, 2026-09-28). The site's Petrona has no small-caps glyphs at all, so the browser SYNTHESIZES small caps by shrinking capitals to 70% (its computed 18px renders as 8px of ink); the plugin's Source Serif 4 Bold has REAL smcp glyphs, which render taller per unit font-size than a synthesized cap does. Option A (18px, matching the site's COMPUTED value) put real smcp glyphs at a size chosen for fake ones, rendering about 25% taller than the site. 15px of real smcp renders the site's own 8px of ink -- this pair's computed font-size now targets the RENDERED match, not the computed one, and 15px vs the site's 18px is the deliberate, measured consequence, not a miss to close.

SC-235 -- a pure CONSEQUENCE of the :font-size entry above, not an independent miss. Both sides run the same 1.7 ratio (site 1.7 x 18px = 30.6px; plugin 1.7 x 15px = 25.5px, inherited from the Plan 21 card-root rule). It is listed separately only because the gate reports per rule.

FOLLOWUPS #39 -- the site's statblock block rhythm is 34px (.sb-wrap margin: 1.7rem auto at the 20px rem base); the plugin's host carries the unscoped base's 0.5em = 8px. SC-110 fixed the half of #39 the gate owned (this pair did not exist, so the site's block margin was invisible to the contract); the residual 34-vs-8 is the real miss #39 recorded and it is a PIXEL decision. Plan 21 Task 2 set the precedent for closing it (it ported the site's 24px .sc-ability margin onto the feature host, Steel-scoped and screen-only, styles-source.css ~3497), but 26px of new air around every statblock and featureblock in an Obsidian note is Scott's call, not a gate ticket's.
FOLLOWUPS #39 -- same finding as statblock-wrap:margin-top (site 34px, plugin 8px); listed separately only because the gate reports per rule.

FOLLOWUPS #39 -- same finding as statblock-wrap:margin-top, on the featureblock family (site .fb-wrap margin: 1.7rem auto = 34px, steel-featureblock.css:41; plugin host 0.5em = 8px). pairs.why: card plate: gradient + bevel + hairline. The plugin side is the HOST div — pipeline.ts stamps data-dse-element on the same root theme.ts stamps data-dse-theme on, and styles-source.css puts the plate there; .dse-feature is an inner content div with no plate.
boxed panel surface

sheen gradient + hairline + the strip's INSET. The site's .sc-ability__section-head is a text-LESS flex wrapper (a .sc-ability__dia diamond + a .tag span); the plugin emits no wrapper at all, so .dse-section__title is simultaneously the strip AND the text. This pair therefore owns only the BOX/MATERIAL rules, which are the ones the wrapper really carries (padding .5rem .9rem = 10/18px, the sheen, the --fx-metal-faint bottom hairline). The type/ink rules are owned by `section-tag` against the site's real text node — reading them off a wrapper that paints no glyphs was FOLLOWUPS #40.

the TEXT the site actually paints in the section head (steel-ability-cards.css:186-187: Newzald small-caps, lowercase, .1em tracking, .9rem, --fx-metal-bright). The plugin's .dse-section__title IS this node's counterpart — it carries the same --dse-metal-bright ink and the same small-caps/lowercase treatment — so the type and ink rules belong here, against glyphs, not against the wrapper's inherited body defaults (FOLLOWUPS #40).
flat right-rail slot: hairline + .35em radius + small-caps, no fill/shadow

power-roll head sheen + inset. Like `section-head` this site node is a text-less flex wrapper (a diamond + .pre + .chars) and the plugin's .dse-pr__head is one node holding the whole caption. The caption LINE's metrics (size, leading, tracking, inset) are the wrapper's, so they stay here; only `ink` moves to `pr-chars`, because the plugin paints the whole caption at the emphasis the site reserves for .chars.

the roll readout — the site's focus text in the power-roll head (steel-ability-cards.css:163). The plugin's single-node caption is deliberately painted at heading emphasis to mirror THIS node rather than the wrapper's inherited body ink, so this is the only honest node to compare its colour against (FOLLOWUPS #40). The residual difference is declared, not measured away.
tier-coloured wash
card head typography

statblock plate. The site plate is .md-typeset.sb (steel-statblock.css:76) — .sb-wrap is an unstyled positioning wrapper, so pairing it monitored nothing. Plugin plate is .dse-sb (the statblock host is deliberately transparent).

BLOCK RHYTHM (FOLLOWUPS #39) — and, since the SC-110 fix round, everything else this node carries. The site's statblock separates from its neighbours on .sb-wrap (margin: 1.7rem auto, steel-statblock.css:68), one level ABOVE the plate the `statblock` pair compares — so until this pair existed no selector in the contract could see the site's block margin at all. It originally narrowed `owns` to the two margin rules on the grounds that everything else on .sb-wrap is unstyled positioning (position/max-width/custom props) and the plate rules live on `statblock`; because its plugin selector is named by no other pair, that narrowing DROPPED 13 rules with no error — and two of them were real (line-height 27.2 vs 24, both schemes, now declared as FOLLOWUPS #52). `owns` is gone: this pair compares the full rule list against the transparent host, and every residual is declared rather than invisible. The plate rules also stay on `statblock`, against a different plugin node, so nothing is double-counted.
role-gradient header band (steel-statblock.css:90)

featureblock PLATE. The site plate is .md-typeset.fb (steel-featureblock.css:44, deliberately margin:0); the plugin collapses wrap+plate into the HOST div, so the plate rules compare here and the block margin moves to `featureblock-wrap`. Comparing the site plate's margin:0 against the host's block margin was the wrong-node reading filed as FOLLOWUPS #39 (it demanded a shrink to 0, the opposite of the real miss).

BLOCK RHYTHM only (FOLLOWUPS #39). The site's featureblock separates from its neighbours on .fb-wrap (margin: 1.7rem auto, steel-featureblock.css:41). The plugin has no wrap node — the host is both — so the margin rules aim here while every other rule stays on the `featureblock` plate pair.
role/malice-gradient header band (steel-featureblock.css:57)

reference-card plate (kit/condition/ancestry/treasure/... via CardLayout). The site node is the .sc-card tile (steel-redesign.css:159-166: --fx-card-bg + --fx-bevel + lift shadow + hairline); its field grammar (__head/__name/__type/__flavor/__stats/__body) is the same one DisplayCardView emits as __title/__subtitle/__badges/__flavor/__rows/__body. Verified against the live pages: the detail pages are NOT the counterpart — a kit detail page is one .sc-kit page-plate and condition/ancestry/treasure detail pages carry no sc- card node at all — so urls.json gained the kit index (tiles) + the perk index (the .sc-card--wide variant, which only re-lays-out the same plate).

SC-232 (card-head NAME type scale) — the generic family: kit/trait/ancestry/class/rule heads and every nested sub-feature, none of which the `head` pair's wrapper-level comparison (.sc-head <-> .dse-head) can see. The kit page's OWN head (steel-cardhead.css:99-101, unscoped by any family override) is the representative generic node on both sides; its plugin counterpart is the direct-child chain that keeps the kit's own head out of its nested signature-ability card (Devastating Rush, a DIFFERENT family at a DIFFERENT size on the same page).

SC-232 — the standalone ability card family (steel-ability-cards.css:107-110). Both selectors require the DIRECT child chain from the card root, which is what keeps a NESTED sub-feature (a different family, generic-sized) from matching either side.
SC-232 — the statblock band family (steel-statblock.css:141-143). Same direct-child scoping reasoning as `name-ability`; a nested sub-feature's head is not a direct child of `.dse-sb`.
SC-232 — the featureblock band family (steel-featureblock.css:85-87). Same direct-child scoping reasoning as `name-ability`.
